metadata.title: The Lighthouse beyond Earth — B1
metadata.synopsis: Em uma estação lunar, Anik encontra um sinal que parece escutar e escolhe como responder antes de automatizar o posto.

scenes.title: A Signal before the Change
scenes.narration: Anik was preparing a lunar communications outpost for automatic operation. Soon, recorded messages would replace his night shifts. While checking the signal desk, he noticed a yellow indicator pulsing three times, followed by a pause. The pattern did not match the station's usual messages. He listened through the headphones, with grey ground and black sky beyond the window. Before handing the room over to a repeating recording, he wanted to know whether something was already trying to be heard.
scenes.prompt: Why did Anik investigate before switching to automatic operation?

options.text: The yellow indicator proved that a visitor was standing outside
The station's usual recordings had already explained the pattern
The unfamiliar pattern might be an incoming attempt to communicate

scenes.explanation: The unfamiliar pattern might be an incoming message. Anik wants to investigate before filling the channel with recordings.

scenes.title: A Pause That Changed
scenes.narration: Anik sent the station's ordinary test tone. The three-beat pattern stopped. When he ended the tone, it returned, but the pause was now longer. He checked the recording twice. A loose connection might repeat a noise, yet this change seemed related to what he had just sent. He wrote down that observation without naming its source. If the response was deliberate, a channel filled with automatic messages might prevent them from hearing each other.
scenes.prompt: What made Anik consider the possibility of a deliberate response?

options.text: The pattern changed after he sent the test tone
The recording announced the name of its sender
The window showed someone holding a transmitter

scenes.explanation: The pause changes after Anik sends a test tone. This suggests a response without proving its source.

scenes.title: A First Reply
scenes.narration: The desk recorder could send either a short spoken message or the same three beats. A voice would show that someone was listening, though the receiver might not understand the words. Repeating the pattern would use a form the unknown source already seemed to recognise. Anik could record either reply and preserve the result for the incoming crew. He kept the automatic transmitter silent and chose how to begin, knowing that a response would still not tell him who was there.
scenes.prompt: What was the advantage of repeating the three beats?

options.text: It guaranteed that the sender would identify itself
It used a form the unknown source seemed to recognise
It allowed the automatic transmitter to fill the channel

scenes.explanation: Repeating the pattern uses a form the receiver seems to recognise. Spoken words might not be understood.

scenes.title: Someone Is Listening
scenes.narration: Anik recorded a simple greeting: "This is Anik. Someone is listening." After he sent it, the speaker returned a broken version of the last two words. He saved both recordings and left clear notes for the incoming crew. There was no name, image or explanation of the distance between them. Still, a reply had changed with his message. He postponed the automatic broadcast. His last night shift had become the start of a conversation that another person could continue.
scenes.prompt: What did the returned words support?

options.text: That Anik knew the sender's identity and location
That the incoming crew no longer needed his recordings
That the reply had changed in relation to Anik's message

scenes.explanation: The returned words change with his greeting. They support a connection, but give no identity or location.

scenes.title: A Pattern for the Next Shift
scenes.narration: Anik sent three beats and waited. The speaker replied with three beats, then a fourth. He repeated the four-beat pattern; the next reply added one more. He saved the exchange and prepared a careful report for the incoming crew. It showed a developing response, not the identity of a sender. He left the channel free of automatic speech. Before leaving the room, he listened once more, comforted by the thought that curiosity could be shared without a common language.
scenes.prompt: Why did Anik describe the exchange cautiously?

options.text: It showed a response but did not identify the sender
It contained only the station's old automatic speech
It proved that the incoming crew had sent every beat

scenes.explanation: The growing pattern shows a developing response. It does not say who is sending it.

visualContinuity.characters: Anik, a 43-year-old man with a long face, medium brown skin, dark eyes, short black hair greying at the temples, a plain slate-blue work shirt, charcoal trousers and soft grey station boots.
visualContinuity.locations: A fictional lunar communications outpost: one control room with a signal desk, a speaker and headphones, a yellow indicator, a recorded-transmission unit, and a wide window onto grey ground and a black sky. Earth is not shown in the window.
visualContinuity.clues: A yellow indicator pulses at the signal desk. An incoming three-beat pattern pauses when the local test stops. A recorder can preserve either a simple spoken greeting or a repeated pulse response. No alien body, face or ship is established.

authoringNotes.learningFocus: Inferência apoiada em resposta observável, limites da evidência e escolha de comunicação. Tecnologia especulativa, sem exigir conhecimento científico externo.
authoringNotes.proposedAudience: Adultos aprendendo inglês; sem violência gráfica. Faixa etária não é um recurso implementado no site.
authoringNotes.reviewStatus: Produção e envio à VPS concluídos: WAVs gerados a partir do texto exato e conferidos por transcrição automática; artes 2D dark inspecionadas e corrigidas por cena. Grafo e questões verificados pelos testes. Não declara revisão auditiva humana nem certificação CEFR.
authoringNotes.supportedGameplay: Cenas, narração pré-gravada, uma pergunta por cena, uma bifurcação e dois finais. Objetos, tecnologias e ações são elementos da ficção; não requerem inventário, fala do jogador, combate ou novos eventos de gameplay.
authoringNotes.levelNote: Nível e tamanho são propostas editoriais, não certificação automática CEFR.
humanReviewChecklist: Revisar compreensão e naturalidade do inglês no nível indicado.
Revisar se cada pergunta tem exatamente uma resposta apoiada no texto.
Revisar continuidade, motivação, tom e ambos os finais.
Revisar o registro de autoria e autorização do texto; preencher créditos e evidências das mídias que forem produzidas.
Produzir e escutar WAVs a partir de audioText; revisar e produzir as imagens-base e loops.
Importar como rascunho, validar mídia no servidor e publicar somente após revisão.
